chunks: 607 - It is narrated from al-Sadiq عليه السلام that he said:

Indeed, one day in the late afternoon, the horses were presented before Sulayman ibn Dawud عليه السلام, and he became occupied with looking at them until the sun disappeared behind the veil. So he said to the angels, 'Return the sun to me so that I may perform my salat (prayer) in its time,' and they returned it.

Then he stood, wiped his legs and neck, and ordered his companions—those whose prayer had passed with him—to do the same. That was their wudu (ablution) for the salat (prayer). Then he stood and prayed, and when he finished, the sun set and the stars appeared.

That is the saying of Allah, Mighty and Majestic: 'And We granted to Dawud Sulayman—an excellent servant; indeed, he was oft-returning. When the poised, swift horses were presented before him in the afternoon, he said: Indeed, I loved the love of good things over the remembrance of my Lord until it disappeared behind the veil. Return them to me. Then he began wiping their legs and necks.'

key_terms.الشَّمْسَ: the sun, which had set and was returned for the prayer
key_terms.الصَّافِنَاتُ الْجِيَادُ: the poised and swift horses mentioned in the Qur'anic verse
key_terms.الْعَشِيِّ: the late afternoon or evening time when the horses were presented
key_terms.ذِكْرِ رَبِّي: the remembrance of my Lord, contrasted in the verse with attention to worldly good
key_terms.سُلَيْمَانَ: Sulayman (Solomon), the prophet whose account is being explained
key_terms.صَلَاتِي: my salat (prayer), referring to the prayer Sulayman عليه السلام sought to perform in its proper time
key_terms.وُضُوءَهُمْ: their wudu (ablution), described here as their purification for prayer

ai.seo_question: How does this hadith explain the Qur'anic verses about Sulayman عليه السلام and the horses in Surah Sad?
ai.summary: This narration explains the verses about Sulayman ibn Dawud عليه السلام by presenting them as referring to his concern for performing salat (prayer) within its proper time. It describes the return of the sun as a divine sign and interprets the wiping mentioned in the verse in connection with preparation for prayer. The report thus combines the story of a prophet’s devotion with tafsir of the Qur'anic passage.
